thumbnail_brief: A pleasant round beach tree with small green apples and a red band painted round its trunk stands in a tropical shower while Doug sits underneath, smiling and dry with his red cap on, rain running off the leaves onto him, with the words WRONG TREE, so the title gives the frame (deadly plants that look harmless) and the thumbnail gives the boss; flat cartoon pink at most, no blisters, rashes, burns or smiling plants, and no PLANT, DEADLY or HARMLESS on the image. Variant B: the same banded tree in a downpour with sap-laden drops falling on Doug as he turns flat pink and looks up, JUST RAIN. Variant C: Doug stirring a soup pot at a campfire, a white-umbelled water hemlock root in his basket and the field guide's EDIBLE? box ticked YES, NOT PARSNIP.
description:
The deadliest plants often look completely harmless: a wild carrot lookalike, a churchyard tree, sweet black berries, a roadside shrub, honey, a glass of milk and a friendly beach tree. Doug meets nine poisonous plants, from water hemlock to the manchineel, each one needing less contact than the last.

Where should we send Doug next? Tell us in the comments.
Subscribe and watch Doug's death counter keep climbing.

— TIMESTAMPS —
{{CHAPTERS}}

— KEY SOURCES —
USDA Agricultural Research Service, water hemlock, the most violently toxic plant in North America: https://www.ars.usda.gov/Research/docs.htm?docid=9996
Cornell Animal Health Diagnostic Center (2024), Taxus (yew) toxicosis in cattle: https://www.vet.cornell.edu/about-us/news/20240220/taxus-spp-toxicosis
Jansen et al. (2012), Cardiovascular Toxicology, grayanotoxin poisoning from mad honey: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3404272
National Park Service, Nancy Hanks Lincoln and milk sickness: https://www.nps.gov/liho/learn/historyculture/nancy.htm
Gilding et al. (2020), Science Advances, the gympie-gympie's pain toxins: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7494335
Guinness World Records, the manchineel as the most dangerous tree: https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/most-dangerous-tree

— DISCLAIMER —
Educational entertainment, not foraging or medical advice. Every death in this video is a cartoon depiction of a stick figure; the science is real and sourced above.

— AI USE —
The narration is an AI text-to-speech voice. Scripts are researched and written with AI assistance and fact-checked against the sources above. All drawings are original.
